correctness.rationale: Direct integration yields Bh=(sin(theta),1-cos(theta))/omega, Ah a rotation by theta=omega*h. The exact Gram matrix is r^2[[1,cos(theta)],[cos(theta),1]], r=2|sin(theta/2)|/omega. Diagonalizing gives both exact singular values and det(W)=4sin^2(theta/2)sin(theta)/omega^2; Taylor expansion at every positive m*pi proves the parity-specific asymptotics. Independent NumPy SVD tests checked 15 nonresonant instances and 36 detuning ratios (maximum singular-value deviation 8.9e-16). These numerical tests are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: The precise, parity-dependent inverse gain of the actual two-step zero-order-hold reachability matrix quantifies a meaningful sampling-design obstruction and distinguishes rank-one resonances from zero-input resonances. It is a motivated exact local conditioning result tied to an explicitly used tracking inverse, not a generic assertion that sampled controllability can fail.

final_claim: For the exact zero-order-hold planar oscillator with A=omega[[0,-1],[1,0]], B=e1 and omega>0, the reachability matrix [Bh,AhBh] loses rank precisely at h=m*pi/omega (positive m). Its least singular value has sharp linear zeros at odd m and quadratic zeros at even m, with constants sqrt(2) and omega/sqrt(2) in h-detuning.
limitations: Fixed omega>0, two state dimensions, one held input, exact zero-order-hold and positive sampling periods; not arbitrary plants.
The nilpotent static-feedback result is not challenged.
